title: How Baku highlighted McLaren’s straight line weakness
excerpt:
For the third time this year after China and Canada, McLaren failed to score a point in Azerbaijan as they endured a painful afternoon.

The huge frustration was that Oscar Piastri had enjoyed his best showing thus far of a troubled 2026 season, and the Australian looked set to log a podium finish, having run second for much of the race.

However, a mistake in the closing laps saw him head down the Turn 1 escape road, and given that the field had been bunched up by the Safety Car, he tumbled out of the top 10 before he could resume.

Lando Norris meanwhile had a messy weekend, suffering with a PU issue that cost him a little performance on the straights relative to his team mate.

He was at least destined to pick up some consolation points before he became collateral damage after the Franco Colapinto/Pierre Gasly collision. Not only was the World Champion bundled out of the race, he also lost some of the upgraded parts that had been introduced in Baku.

“It's been a very frustrating Saturday,” said Team Principal Andrea Stella. “I think we had issues and some mistakes, but at the same time I think we paid some fundamental limitations of our package in this kind of circuit, because we were not fast enough in the corners.

“But at the same time, mainly we were not fast enough in the straights, and this continuously exposed our drivers to being attacked and having to spend their race pretty much watching the mirrors rather than thinking at how they can progress in the race.”

Stella stressed that Piastri had done a great job in the circumstances, and crucially he appeared to have got on top of the issues that have been hampering him with the 2026 car.

Azerbaijan mistake 'certainly took me by surprise' – Piastri

“Oscar did this sort of defensive race very well,” said Stella. “He was very precise. His race reminded me very much of what he did in 2024 to win the race, when he held [Charles] Leclerc behind for a long time.

“But unfortunately, after the pit stop and having gone on the medium tyres, which were performing worse than the soft tyres, he had a lock-up and his race finished there.

“It's a real shame for Oscar, because he deserved to have a go at fighting for the podium, and also because Oscar has been driving very well the entire weekend. And we know that Oscar was in a little bit of learning trajectory to adapt to the 2026 car, and it would have been good to be rewarded.”

Stella admitted that life was made even harder for Norris by the PU issue that had hindered him in Qualifying, and which didn’t go away.

“If we look at Lando's race and the fact that he gradually went backwards, there's a few reasons for that,” he said. “We occasionally saw the same problem during the race, but not as systematic as in Qualifying.

"It was a little bit intermittent, but definitely there's a significant opportunity on the topic of fuel injection that we saw occasionally also on Oscar's car during the race. So this is a topic that we should look at high priority.

“In addition to that, Lando was overtaken by [Max] Verstappen, that was a quicker car. Lando was struggling a bit with the medium tyres – I mentioned Verstappen because he was on medium tyres as well as Lando, but he was faster. But credit to Oscar, Oscar managed to keep Verstappen behind.

“On Lando's side, we were struggling a little bit with power unit deployment, and also Lando was having some inconsistencies in his driving. When he was overtaken by [Lewis] Hamilton, he had a lock-up, and he had a few mistakes that meant that cars behind were within range. And when they are within range, then we struggle to defend, which goes back to the point on top speed.”

Stella conceded that it was a tricky weekend for Norris: “I would say that for Lando, this was one of the most difficult events in general that he has experienced in 2026, something that we need to take away, looking at whatever can be improved.

“But I would say most of the opportunities lie on the team side, and on the car side, because we need to be able to offer our drivers a car that is more raceable and just more consistent in terms of predictability.”

‘Some drivers shouldn’t be in F1’ – Norris on Baku clash

The top speed equation is always a complicated one, and it’s never just about pure horsepower.

“We need to look, I think, as a team, as to why the car wasn't as competitive as it should be in these long straights,” said Stella. “And it is very apparent that it is not a single factor. Certainly, we have always talked quite openly and transparently that we need to improve the aerodynamic drag of the car.

“There are a few factors, which refer to our ratios for instance – we need to look whether we are on the right ratios to compete in circuits in which you have this sort of top speed.

“And at the same time, when we look at the data and we compare with [Mercedes], we see that our power unit was not optimised. I think, while for Qualifying we managed to exploit pretty much the most that was available in the power unit, there's a few items that we were not able to optimise, and we paid the price in the race. So there's some work to do on the power unit side.”

The Baku upgrade package, which targeted slow-corner performance, delivered encouraging results despite the team's disappointing weekend.

“We are happy," said Stella. "The data seems to confirm that there's no issues with the upgrades, so hopefully there will be more benefit at the coming races. This has been a great effort by the entire team."

He admitted some components may have been lost in the crash but was confident replacements would arrive in time.

“Unfortunately, I think a couple of parts will have been lost with the crash, which is another downside of having been involved in these sorts of situations. But luckily, there's some more new parts coming, so we should be okay for the coming races.”

Stella also confirmed McLaren's development focus has switched to next year's car, with only previously approved updates still due to reach the MCL40.

“There's a tail of parts that will land trackside, so we will see still some new parts coming to the MCL40. But at the moment, as we speak, all the efforts are already concentrated onto next year's car, and what we see coming trackside is the result of parts being released a few weeks ago.”

title: Mekies praises Hadjar's 'outstanding' Baku podium on return
excerpt:
Laurent Mekies has praised Isack Hadjar’s performance in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as “outstanding”, after the Red Bull driver returned from a wrist injury to claim a podium.

Hadjar made his first appearance since sustaining the injury during the summer break, and despite a steady start during practice in Baku to build up confidence, took an impressive fourth in Qualifying.

It also included starting ahead of Red Bull team mate Max Verstappen, and although he let the charging Dutchman through in the opening laps, Hadjar stayed with the four-time World Champion, eventually moving up to third after Oscar Piastri made a mistake at Turn 1 in the closing stages.

“I think it was outstanding what Isack has produced this weekend,” said Team Principal Mekies.

“Really outstanding. At first, the most important thing is that he felt straight away good in the car, no pain. Every time that we met together in the last few weeks we said we will wait for Isack to come back at 100%, because that's the priority.

“Nonetheless, even without pain, it's not an easy track to go back to, because of the no margin for error. And he has been building up his rhythms, session after session, very calmly, with a lot of energy – with a lot of positive energy.”

As well as making his return, Hadjar was also confirmed as being retained by Red Bull for 2027 after a sophomore season where the Frenchman has steadily improved his pace, which includes a podium in Monaco.

Mekies admits he was particularly impressed by Hadjar's calmness during Saturday's race in Baku, after insisting over the radio he didn't want to fight Verstappen and compromise both their races.

“It shows you how cleverly the kid is racing, and how much of brain capacity he is developing while in the car, and how much emotion control he is managing to have," said Mekies.

"And [there are] many indicators of steps he has made in all these areas, on top of producing more speed.

“So it's exactly that trajectory that has been impressing us every day since he has joined the team. Probably last year as well.

"And that's also there that we want to give him the best possible environment for him to continue to develop, because that step was truly impressive.”

title: Alpine release statement over online abuse after Baku race
excerpt:
Alpine have issued a statement speaking out against the “hate and abuse” posted online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, in which their driver Franco Colapinto triggered a multi-car incident.

Colapinto locked up and went too deep at Turn 1 during the first Safety Car restart at the Baku City Circuit, taking out both Alpine team mate Pierre Gasly and the McLaren of Lando Norris.

The Argentinian was subsequently given a 10-second time penalty by the stewards, who converted it into a five-place grid drop for the upcoming Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, given that he did not finish the race.

With the collision sparking debate across social media, Alpine took to their own official channels on Sunday morning to condemn some of the comments that have been made.

“As a team, we feel it’s necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix,” read the Alpine statement.

“Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula 1 community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport.

“Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

“Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

“As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula 1, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

“We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution.

“We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula 1 is renowned for and what makes it so special.”

title: 'I'm one of the best out there and I'm not afraid to say it' – Ocon
excerpt:
Esteban Ocon has insisted he is "one of the best out there" among the current crop of F1 drivers, as he bounced back in style in Baku amid doubts over his Haas future.

It’s been a tough 2026 for the Frenchman and his frustration boiled over on Friday in Azerbaijan when a yellow flag left him in P14 in Qualifying on a day when Q3 was on the cards.

It was the last thing he needed given the speculation surrounding his Haas future in 2027, after he hinted he was "definitely a free agent for next year."

He responded in the best way possible in Saturday’s race by taking his opportunities and avoiding the chaos around him to claim P8 at the flag – his best result of the season thus far, and only his third top-10 finish.

The only disappointment was that it could have been even better had he not lost a spot to Arvid Lindblad on the dash across the line on the last lap.

Despite that his mood couldn’t have been more different than it had been 24 hours earlier.

“Super happy with the result,” said the Frenchman. “When the car is working, that's what we deserve. We had a strong car since the beginning of the weekend. We took all the right decisions, on the pit stop, on the Safety Car.

“So yeah, it's been it's been a really, really good race. I'm really happy with the result, and I think it gives just good, positive vibes for everyone to move forward on that triple [header].

“We are going into a very difficult track with a lot of corners, a lot of high-speed corners, and we showed that we have a car that's pretty competitive. So it should be two exciting races for us. I'm looking forward to them.”

It was the restart after the first Safety Car that helped to propel Ocon into the points. He was in P13 and fighting with Liam Lawson down to Turn 1 when Franco Colapinto, Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris were taken out of contention by a collision.

Already up to P9, into Turn 2 he passed team mate Ollie Bearman, who lost momentum after a touch with Kimi Antonelli.

“I overtook Liam, who was a little bit slow on the line,” said Ocon. “I was mid of the car, he was still in front, but that gave me enough to go into Turn 1. And then I just dived into Turn 2, into Ollie, and got in front of him.”

After the second restart a mistake from Oscar Piastri handed him another place, leaving the two Haas drivers in P7 and P8.

“From there on what was going to be difficult was to keep the overtake in front,” said Ocon.

“And that was not possible, because the quick cars, they just disappeared. So we were playing the team game with Ollie.

“I gave him overtake for the last four or five laps until he got overtaken by Lindblad, unfortunately.”

It looked like Ocon would be able to stay in front of the Racing Bulls, but then he was caught out when Valtteri Bottas crashed in the closing stages.

"Obviously I cut the corner because I didn't know if Valtteri was in the middle of the track,” said Ocon. “I thought I don't want to be at the stewards arguing that I gained an advantage, so I backed off, and I thought that was going to be enough. But they [Racing Bulls] are super-fast in the straight, and I overdid it.”

Lindblad got him on the line to claim the place by just 0.03s. Nevertheless P8 was a timely reward for someone who has never doubted his own ability.

“I've raced with everyone out there, and I've always been on par,” he said. “I've won every championship that I've raced with. I've won races in Formula Renault, I won championships in go-karts, I won Formula 3, I won GP3. I was racing in the top 10 in DTM for half a season, I won in Formula 1. I can do it. I'm one of the best out there and I'm not afraid to say it.”

It was a good day too for Bearman, who was more than happy to claim P9 despite losing out to his team mate at the restart.

“I'm super happy to score points with both cars,” he said. “It's such an incredible feeling, even if it was a race of attrition with a lot of retirements, where I think if it was green, we would have been P11, like where I was.

“However, we'll take it. To stay in a race like this is always the target. We know how crazy they can be, and it was crazy today, and I'm so proud of the entire team, everyone back home at the factory, also in Italy, the aero guys.

“To bring points after the upgrade that we bought, I can't imagine how they're feeling right now – I think they should be very proud of themselves.”

title: Leclerc urges Ferrari to ‘bring upgrades to close the gap’
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc has emphasised the need for Ferrari to “bring upgrades in order to close the gap” to rivals Mercedes, Red Bull and McLaren after enduring a frustrating Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Although the Monegasque’s Qualifying effort was eight tenths adrift of George Russell’s pole position lap, it still earned him a spot on the front row, and Ferrari opted to start him on soft tyres with the aim of taking an early lead.

But over the course of the first stint, Leclerc lost out to Oscar Piastri and both Red Bull drivers as he struggled to match their pace, leaving him to settle for P4 after the Aussie dropped out of the points late in the race.

“They were very strong,” Leclerc reflected. “McLaren were also strong – not maybe as strong as Red Bull, but Red Bull were particularly strong. We know they have a very strong power unit so this is a good race for them, but still.

“We were quite far off Mercedes, far off Red Bull, a bit behind McLaren – these are our competitors and it’s not new. It’s [been] quite a few races now that we’re losing a little bit of track to them, so it's important that we react to that and that we bring upgrades in order to close the gap again.”

Alongside Mercedes, who have set the benchmark for much of the season, the Scuderia chose not to introduce any updates in Baku, while McLaren and Red Bull made changes to their cars.

Their lack of progress at the street circuit left Leclerc to question whether they’ll be able to make a big enough step to beat the other frontrunners and hold onto second place in the Constructors’ Championship.

“We've got things in the pipeline, but I don't know what the others have in the pipeline,” he added. “We are going to improve the car – whether it's going to be enough to outrace them in the development programme… I don't know what they have in store.”

His team mate Lewis Hamilton suffered a similarly lonely race as he failed to move forward from his starting position of P6, with a hard-fought overtake on Lando Norris marking his main highlight before he was later passed by Kimi Antonelli.

Asked whether he was surprised not to take the fight to other cars up ahead, he said: “Not really. I was just surprised all weekend – I couldn't get the tyres working at all.

“Even through the whole race the tyres were just switching on, switching off, switching on, switching off, and so one minute the grip picks up for a second and then it drops away. We were seconds a lap slower than the cars right at the front, so there was nothing I could do.

“It's different at every track. The last track I think we were okay, but for some reason this weekend we couldn't get it working the whole weekend.”

title: Alpine consider 'what action should be taken' after Colapinto crash
excerpt:
Flavio Briatore has said he will take time to "consider what course of action should be taken" after Franco Colapinto's error in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix took both him and team mate Pierre Gasly out of the race, as well as McLaren's Lando Norris.

Saturday's race in Baku had been going positively for the Enstone-based team up until that point, with Gasly holding onto seventh place while Colapinto had been duelling for P9 with Norris, who had just dropped down the order following a lock-up.

However, after a Safety Car was called following Alex Albon's crash, Alpine's afternoon unravelled in spectacular style.

At the restart, Colapinto came into Turn 1 too fast, locked up and speared into the side of his team mate’s car, with Gasly in turn hitting Norris. All three went off, with Gasly and Norris parking up immediately, while the Argentine racer managed to limp his car back to the pits

However, his efforts in bringing the car back was to no avail as the damage was too great for the team to repair. As a result that meant a double DNF on a day where double points had looked incredibly likely, while Norris was left less than impressed.

"At the end of the day, I just got taken out… just some drivers that shouldn’t be in F1, to be honest," said the reigning World Champion after the race.

While Colapinto was quick to hold his hands up over the incident, apologising over the radio before adding further apologies after the race to both the team and Gasly, Briatore was left frustrated with the "very poor move".

“Obviously I'm extremely disappointed with the outcome of today's race, knowing we lost valuable points in the Championship fight,” said Alpine's Executive Advisor.

“These sort of incidents shouldn't happen, particularly when we were running well with both cars in point-scoring positions. I feel very sorry for the team and for Pierre who did a great job all weekend and my apologies also go to Lando [Norris] and McLaren for ruining their race.

“I know that Franco has taken full responsibility for it, as he should; in fact he braked far too late considering the context of the race and the Safety Car restart. It was a very poor move for a driver of his experience.

“I want to take time to reflect on it and consider what course of action should be taken, so we can learn from it and avoid such a situation in future.”

Alpine had been on course to slash the nine-point gap to Racing Bulls for fifth in the teams' standings, but instead have fallen six points further adrift as Arvid Lindblad finished seventh.

Colapinto will also be hindered in next weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia after his 10-second penalty for causing the collision was converted into a five-place grid drop, given the Argentine was unable to serve his in-race penalty after retiring.

“Just a big sorry to all of them, to the factory, to Pierre of course," Colapinto said in the Baku media pen.

"[I] took him out, so really disappointed. We were both in a position to score points, was a big day for the team and [I] did a big mistake. Big sorry, it shouldn't happen.”

Giving his verdict, Gasly added: “I don’t think I really have words and I don’t need the words now. We’ll manage it together as a team.

"I’m obviously very disappointed for all the guys, P7 and P10 was a very good race, good pace. Honestly, I have no idea how to answer your question. [We’ve] got to move on.”

title: The 2026 Qualifying and race head-to-heads so far
excerpt:
As the 2026 season continues, F1.com assesses how the team mate head-to-heads have stacked up so far. Who from each of the 11 pairings on the grid has had the upper hand in Qualifying and/or race trim across the campaign? Let’s take a look at the numbers…

Mercedes

Qualifying: Russell 7-8 Antonelli

Race: Russell 5-10 Antonelli

Perhaps unsurprisingly given his hold on the top spot in the Drivers’ Championship, Kimi Antonelli has also taken the lead when it comes to the head-to-head statistics at Mercedes. The Italian has beaten George Russell in Qualifying eight times out of 15, with six of those occasions seeing him take pole position.

The numbers are similar in the race day figures, Antonelli having crossed the line ahead of Russell at 10 Grands Prix – and winning at eight of them. Russell on the other hand has experienced marginally more bad luck, recording two DNFs in comparison to one for Antonelli.

Russell closed the gap last weekend in Baku, taking pole position and his first victory since Austria in June to close the gap to Antonelli in the drivers' standings to 66 points.

Ferrari

Qualifying: Leclerc 8-7 Hamilton

Race: Leclerc 7-8 Hamilton

Over at Ferrari, there is little to choose between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton on both counts. Leclerc just edged ahead of Hamilton on Qualifying stats after his front row start in Baku, while his fourth-place finish in the race means he has closed on his team mate in race head-to-heads.

McLaren

Qualifying: Norris 9-6 Piastri

Race: Norris 8-6 Piastri*

*No mark included for the Chinese Grand Prix as both drivers failed to start

In the Qualifying statistics between Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, Norris leads the way with nine better results. This includes his pole positions at the Hungarian, Dutch and Spanish Grands Prix.

The McLaren pair aren't too far apart in race day figures, although Norris has recorded three DNFs, while Piastri has one to his name as well as a DNS from the season opener in Australia (not including the Chinese Grand Prix where both recorded a DNS). Norris is responsible for the squad's two victories so far at the Hungaroring and Zandvoort.

Red Bull

Qualifying: Verstappen 8-4 Hadjar

Qualifying: Verstappen 3-0 Lawson

Race: Verstappen 9-3 Hadjar

Race: Verstappen 2-1 Lawson

Isack Hadjar faced the difficult task of stepping up as Max Verstappen’s new team mate at Red Bull in 2026 – and while he has enjoyed a solid start to the campaign, it is the Dutchman that leads the way in the statistics.

Verstappen has outqualified his team mate on eight occasions, as well as finishing ahead on race day nine times. The four-time World Champion recorded retirements at the other three events, one more DNF than the two experienced by Hadjar.

The Frenchman was unexpectedly replaced by Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson for the Dutch Grand Prix after sustaining a wrist injury, and while Verstappen narrowly beat the New Zealander in Qualifying, he suffered a massive crash at the start of the race to mark his fourth DNF of the season.

Lawson brought it home in seventh place, scoring points on his first appearance for the team since he was demoted shortly into the 2025 season, and scored points again in Madrid before Hadjar's return in Baku.

It was a strong comeback for Hadjar, who beat Verstappen in qualifying before finishing behind his more experienced team mate in the race to claim his second podium of the season.

Racing Bulls

Qualifying: Lawson 7-5 Lindblad

Qualifying: Tsunoda 0-3 Lindblad

Race: Lawson 8-4 Lindblad

Race: Tsunoda 1-2 Lindblad

The first half of the season has been strong for Racing Bulls, with both drivers performing well. However, it is Lawson who has taken the lead in the head-to-heads, albeit narrowly in Qualifying form – the New Zealander holding the edge by sevent to five over Arvid Lindblad.

Lawson has finished ahead of Lindblad at eight out of the 12 Grands Prix they have contested for Racing Bulls, though the gap between the duo – who have recorded five double points finishes so far – has often been small. There has been one retirement so far for Lawson (in Miami), while Lindblad did not start in Canada due to a clutch issue.

Their run of seven rounds with at least one driver in the top 10 came to an end in Zandvoort, where reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda stepped in for Lawson. The Japanese racer had never driven the 2026 cars before, making it even more impressive that he came close to scoring as he improved from P12 on the grid – two positions behind Lindblad – to P11.

Tsunoda remained with the team in Monza and did add a point to their tally, with Lindblad also returning to the top 10 in what proved a strong weekend for the team.

Lindblad and the returning Lawson collided in Baku last time out, before the former went on to finish P7 and claim his 10th points finish of the season during an impressive rookie campaign.

Alpine

Qualifying: Gasly 12-3 Colapinto

Race: Gasly 9-5 Colapinto *No mark for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as both drivers retired

Pierre Gasly has been dominant in the Qualifying statistics at Alpine, having beaten Franco Colapinto by 12 to three.

He even grabbed his maiden pole position at Monza, completely on merit in a dry session as the upgraded Alpine took the fight to the top teams.

The picture is a little more even on race day, where Gasly’s lead is now nine over Colapinto’s five. The French driver could not back up his pole position at Monza with a podium, but did come home seventh with his team mate also scoring in ninth.

The pair were on course for a double points finish in Baku, but a crash between the pair after a Safety Car restart, with Colapinto handed a five-place grid penalty, meant a double DNF.

Haas

Qualifying: Bearman 10-5 Ocon

Race: Bearman 8-6 Ocon*

*No mark for the Dutch Grand Prix as both drivers retired

At Haas, Ollie Bearman has qualified ahead of Esteban Ocon on 10 occasions. The Briton’s best Saturday result so far was a P10 in China, and also last time out in Baku.

Bearman has the edge in Grand Prix finishes too, beating Ocon by eight to six. In terms of reliability, Bearman has suffered four DNFs, with Ocon experiencing his first of the year in Zandvoort as neither were able to finish the race.

Ocon achieved his best result of the season with P8 in Azerbaijan, as Bearman's P9 meant Haas secured its first double points finsh of the season.

Audi

Qualifying: Hulkenberg 7-8 Bortoleto

Race: Hulkenberg 7-8 Bortoleto

Audi drivers Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto are almost evenly matched when it comes to Qualifying performances, with Bortoleto claiming their best starting position of P8 at the Belgian Grand Prix.

It is also Bortoleto who marginally has the better race day statistics, the Brazilian finishing ahead of Hulkenberg at eight of the 15 rounds so far. The younger driver has enjoyed better luck in terms of reliability; Bortoleto has crossed the line at every race barring China – where he failed to start – while Hulkenberg has suffered three DNFs along with a DNS in Australia.

Williams

Qualifying: Albon 5-10 Sainz

Race: Albon 6-9 Sainz

It has been a tough campaign so far for Williams, who remain down in P9 of the Teams’ Championship. While there has not been much to celebrate, Carlos Sainz might take heart from the fact that he has led the Qualifying head-to-head by 10 to five over Alex Albon.

That does not quite tell the full story though, with Albon offering his team mate a tow in Monza to ensure Sainz made it to Q2, while the Spaniard lost a top-10 start in Baku due to a grid penalty.

Sainz also tops the Grand Prix figures, by nine to six. Points have been a rarity for the team, with the Spaniard recording three P9 finishes, and most recently a P10 in Baku with a heavily upgraded car, while Albon has a P8 and a P10 to his name.

Aston Martin

Qualifying: Alonso 13-2 Stroll

Race: Alonso 8-2 Stroll*

*No mark for the Australian, Chinese, Barcelona, Italian and Azerbaijan Grands Prix as both drivers retired

Like Williams, Aston Martin have endured a challenging 2026. Such were the squad’s car issues that neither driver was able to finish the opening two rounds in Australia and China, while both also retired with reliability problems in Barcelona and Baku. However, substantial upgrades to the car and power unit have offered encouraging signs of progress.

In terms of the head-to-heads, Fernando Alonso has outscored Lance Stroll on both counts – albeit by a lesser extent on Sundays – and the Spaniard is also responsible for the team’s three points as he finished P10 in Monaco and P9 in the Netherlands.

Cadillac

Qualifying: Perez 8-7 Bottas

Race: Perez 9-4 Bottas*

*No mark for the Austrian and Hungarian Grands Prix as both drivers retired

Cadillac recruited the experienced pairing of Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez for the squad’s maiden F1 season – and while the duo have often been fighting towards the rear of the pack, Perez got the better of Bottas in Baku and moved ahead on their Qualifying figures so far.

The Mexican also holds the advantage in the Grand Prix statistics, finishing ahead of Bottas on nine occasions. Both drivers have suffered their fair share of reliability concerns, with the Finn retiring from six races while Perez is on five DNFs.

title: George Russell fights back as Franco Colapinto sparks mayhem - Azerbaijan GP winners & losers
excerpt:
It was a remarkable weekend for George Russell and Isack Hadjar, in particular, but what a disaster for Alpine!

George Russell held off a late charge from Max Verstappen to win an Azerbaijan Grand Prix heavily disrupted by two safety cars, with a Turn 1 pile-up on the first restart wiping out both Alpine drivers and Lando Norris in one move.

Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar took his first 'proper' podium on his return from injury, while Haas banked another double-points finish courtesy of Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman.

Here are the winners and losers from Baku.

© XPBimages

Winner - George Russell

Russell converted pole into victory, building a lead of more than 10 seconds before Alex Albon's Turn 5 crash brought out the first safety car.

The Mercedes driver then had to defend twice from restarts, and nearly came unstuck on the final lap when he lifted for a yellow flag at Turn 15 and lost turbo power, letting Verstappen close to within 0.196 seconds at the chequered flag.

It was Russell's eighth win of his F1 career, his third this season, and his first lights-to-flag success. The British driver came so close to a 'super' grand chelem after topping the first two practice sessions, and all three qualifying sessions en route to taking pole before claiming the fastest lap en route to victory. Only Verstappen denied him late on in FP3.

Russell has now closed the gap on team-mate Kimi Antonelli to 66 points at the top of the drivers' standings. It was a nervy finish, but a win is a win.

© Red Bull Content Pool

Winner - Isack Hadjar

Hadjar delivered his best weekend since returning from a six-week wrist injury, running an effective offset strategy on soft tyres and staying close to team-mate Verstappen throughout the opening stint.

Red Bull's decision to hold track position rather than swap the pair paid off once the safety cars fell his way as he capitalised when Oscar Piastri fumbled a restart, moving past the McLaren into third.

The result, achieved days after his Red Bull contract for next year was confirmed, was his first genuine podium finish, given the confusion around the one scored in Monaco. It was a timely reminder of why Red Bull backed him for next year.

© XPBimages

Winner - Haas

Haas again turned chaos into points, starting both cars on soft tyres before pitting Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman for mediums under the lap 30 safety car.

The pair then rode the second round of restarts to move up into eighth and ninth, a double finish that pushed Haas 10 points clear of Audi in the battle for seventh in the constructors' table.

This is becoming a pattern for the American outfit, which remains among the sharpest strategic operators in the midfield on chaotic afternoons. Baku suited them perfectly.

© XPBimages

Loser - Alpine

Alpine's afternoon fell apart at the worst possible moment when Franco Colapinto locked up under braking on the first restart and collided with team-mate Pierre Gasly into Turn 1.

Both cars were eliminated on the spot, and the clash also collected Lando Norris, turning what had been a promising midfield battle into a written-off weekend for the Enstone squad.

Colapinto was handed a five-place grid penalty for the upcoming Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia in place of a 10-second time penalty he could not serve in Baku.

It was a double DNF that could scarcely have been more costly, with Alpine losing ground on Racing Bulls in the constructors' standings, and what next for Colapinto after team boss Flavio Briatore said he would "consider what course of action" to take with his driver?

© XPBimages

Loser - Lando Norris

Norris' weekend soured in qualifying, when a moment off-track triggered a yellow flag and compromised his final lap, leaving him down in fifth on the grid.

Worse followed in the race, as he was collected in the Turn 1 pile-up caused by Colapinto's lock-up, ending his afternoon immediately.

The McLaren driver was later scathing about the standard of driving that caused the incident and called for the FIA to consider race bans for such carelessness.

Such comments later resulted in Norris being the latest target in F1 for online abuse from angry Colapinto fans.

Loser - Alex Albon

Albon's race ended in a barrier at Turn 5 on lap 31, an accident that triggered the first safety car and reshuffled the entire complexion of the afternoon.

With the Williams of Albon and team-mate Carlos Sainz sporting a raft of updates, ending the race with a heavily damaged car was a major setback for the team, which has endured a torrid season.

Whilst Sainz at least managed to salvage a point for the team by finishing 10th, ending a run of nine races outside the points, Albon extended his own pointless streak to nine with a weekend to forget in Baku.

title: Defiant Esteban Ocon fights for F1 future: 'I'm one of the best out there'
excerpt:
Esteban Ocon has staunchly defended his place in F1, insisting he is "one of the best out there" after his future was thrown into serious doubt heading into 2027.

Ocon is understood to have already been informed he will not continue with Haas next season, with the American outfit actively evaluating alternatives, including Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, who has emerged as the frontrunner to partner Oliver Bearman.

The French driver used the Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend to confirm his situation publicly, revealing he holds no contract for next year.

"At the moment, I'm definitely a free agent for next year," Ocon said in the Baku paddock during his Wednesday media session.

"There are things in discussion that are out of my control. There are certain topics that are out of my control. So, I will keep pushing until the end of the year and see how it goes."

Asked whether staying with Haas remains a possibility, the 30-year-old simply responded: "Let's see."

Ocon 'not afraid' to make his case

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu played down suggestions that a call had already been made, maintaining that an option date on Ocon had simply passed without resolution.

"Every driver has a clause at a certain point in the year to decide on an option. It just means that we haven't decided on that option yet, but that was quite a long time ago, so his situation hasn't really changed," Komatsu said. "We're still trying to finalise what we're going to do for next year."

Ocon's campaign alongside Bearman has been a difficult one, with the Briton having routinely got the better of his more experienced team-mate and established the upper hand.

But an eighth-place finish in Baku, one place ahead of Bearman, gave Ocon fresh ammunition to argue his case.

"I can say, 'I deserve that', not all the rest of the shit," Ocon told media, including RacingNews365, when it was put to him that the result was redemption during a tough spell.

When he was asked if the result proved he can deliver when the VF-26 performs, he replied, "Yeah" before launching an impassioned plea for his place in F1.

"I've raced with everyone out there, and I've always been on par," Ocon stated. "I've won in every championship that I've raced in. I won races in Formula Renault. I won championships in go-karts. I won Formula 3. I won GP3.

"I was racing in the top 10 in DTM for half the season. I've won in Formula 1. I can do it.

"I'm one of the best out there, and I'm not afraid to say it."

title: Alpine forced to condemn online abuse again after Franco Colapinto-sparked chaos
excerpt:
Alpine has issued a fresh public condemnation of online abuse after a collision triggered by Franco Colapinto wiped out three cars at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto lost control of his Alpine into Turn 1 at the Baku City Circuit following a safety car restart, collecting team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris in the process. All three retired on the spot.

The incident has since triggered a wave of hostile reaction online, notably towards Norris and Colapinto. The backlash has also extended to members of the Formula 1 media and to rival competitors caught up in the incident.

It is the second time this year that Alpine has felt compelled to speak out. The team published an open letter in April, following the Japanese Grand Prix, condemning online hate directed at Colapinto and acknowledging it had been slow to respond to abuse and death threats aimed at former driver Esteban Ocon after a collision between the pair in China.

In May last year, the team issued a statement calling out abuse after former driver Jack Doohan and his family were targeted online.

Alpine - It has become a regular occurrence

In the latest statement issued by Alpine, the team said it felt it necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse circulating online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

It said the abuse was aimed "not only at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula One community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport.

"Mistakes happen when racing at the limit, and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

"As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

"We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution.

"We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula One is renowned for and what makes it so special."

title: Max Verstappen denies George Russell super-rare F1 achievement only Lewis Hamilton holds
excerpt:
George Russell came painstakingly close to clinching a seldom-attained feat during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend, something only Lewis Hamilton has achieved.

George Russell fell agonisingly short of a Super Grand Chelem at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, after Max Verstappen beat him to top spot in the final free practice session in Baku.

Russell topped FP1 and FP2, then took pole position in qualifying before leading every lap of Sunday's race to claim victory and the fastest lap, completing a standard Grand Chelem in the process.

Had he also finished quickest across all three practice sessions and all three qualifying segments, he would have joined an extremely exclusive club.

But Verstappen denied him that distinction in FP3 on Friday morning, setting a time of 1:43.922 to beat Russell's 1:44.021 by just under a tenth of a second.

It meant the Mercedes driver's run of topping every session of the weekend was broken at the first hurdle of Friday running, even as he went on to sweep Q1, Q2 and Q3 before dominating the grand prix itself.

Hamilton's benchmark stands alone

The Super Grand Chelem, though not an officially recognised FIA classification, has been achieved only once since the current three-part qualifying format was introduced in 2006.

Lewis Hamilton managed the feat at the 2015 Italian Grand Prix, topping every practice and qualifying session at Monza before winning from pole and setting the fastest lap, though Mercedes did face a post-race tyre pressure query that the stewards ultimately dismissed.

Daniel Ricciardo also came close in 2018, securing pole, victory and every lap led in Monaco, but a mid-race MGU-K failure cost his Red Bull roughly a quarter of its power and left him managing brakes and fuel for the remainder of the race. The resulting pace deficit ruled out any chance of the fastest lap that weekend.

title: Christian Horner hands Red Bull damning verdict after exit: 'Lost its vibe'
excerpt:
Christian Horner believes Red Bull no longer has the same "vibe" following his exit from the F1 team 15 months ago.

After 20 years as team principal, Horner was axed in July last year for reasons he claims he still does not fully understand, although it is claimed he was given a hefty pay-off, with reported figures varying between £50 million and £80 million.

In an interview with The Times, Horner made clear he is not at liberty to discuss the minutiae of his departure; however, he does feel that Red Bull is no longer the team it once was now he is no longer in charge.

Horner feels that whatever the number behind his pay-off, "it demonstrates that you’ve done nothing wrong".

He added: "They just don’t want you any more. If somebody’s prepared to pay that much money for you not to be there…"

After a pause, he then offers a clear point of view on the state of Red Bull at present by declaring, "And I think if you look at that team 12 months down the line, it’s lost its mojo, its presence, its vibe."

[Article continues below]

Christian Horner Racing?

As to why he left, Horner seems to think the powers that be at Red Bull felt he had become too much of a domineering presence and the team was losing its identity.

Notably, of course, Horner had hit the headlines for all the wrong reasons in 2024 when a female employee at the team accused him of controlling and coercive behaviour, sparking two internal investigations.

Arguably, Red Bull's decline in performance in the first half of 2025 is understood to have played a part, although it is something Horner disputes.

Asked as to why he felt he was fired, Horner replied: "I was never given a clear explanation other than that they felt the performance had slipped a little.

"Even though at the [previous] race we’d been on pole position and leading the British Grand Prix; had it not been for the weather, we’d probably have won it.

"And that they wanted to go in a different direction. When I really pushed - I had six years left on my contract - I was told that it was more Christian Horner Racing than Red Bull Racing."

title: Kimi Antonelli reveals mindset shift as he 'drove like his grandmother'
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has conceded to 'driving like his grandmother' during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, whilst there was also a change in his mindset given the circumstances he faced.

Antonelli endured a difficult few days around the Baku City Circuit, initially suffering a hydraulics issue in first practice that led to the loss of valuable track time for the remainder of that session and a portion of FP2 following a power unit change.

The 20-year-old Italian then made a rare mistake this season that led to him crashing in the first part of qualifying and lining up 16th on the grid. Antonelli even dropped a place to 17th after the opening lap.

There was no charge to the front, as was the case in Monza three weeks previously when Antonelli won the Italian Grand Prix from 19th; instead, Antonelli finished fifth, losing 15 points to team-mate George Russell, who has cut the lead to 66 points.

"I was driving a bit like my grandmother, just damage save mode," said Antonelli, speaking to the media, including RacingNews365.

"I didn't take any risks. Before making a move, I made sure that I could go for it. All in all, it's one of those days where you have to be happy with P5."

[Article continues below]

Antonelli sustained 'big damage'

Antonelli confirmed he opted to alter his approach to the race as it evolved.

"Yes, definitely," he said. "If I'd had the same pace as at Monza, or in previous races, it would have been different. It would have been just full attack.

"But I realised very early that, first of all, it was a lot harder to overtake with a train of cars all in overtake mode, and then I didn't have the same pace as I'd had previously, so the mindset changed very quickly.

"And also, seeing so many people making mistakes, I pulled back a little because I just wanted to take advantage of everyone else's mistake and just move forward."

Antonelli's cause was not aided later on at the first safety car restart, following Alex Albon ploughing his Williams into a barrier, when he tangled with the Haas of Ollie Bearman.

Alpine's Franco Colapinto made a move into Turn 1 that took out his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris, whilst there were also unintended consequences for Antonelli.

"I saw the Alpine locking up, and I pulled back immediately," said Antonelli. "I was getting ready to do a switchback, but then I didn't see Ollie coming so quickly on the inside.

"I had to cut because I was still very close to the Alpine when I switched back, but I had big floor damage. The whole left side was gone with the contact, and after that, the car was very sketchy to drive.

"Obviously, I was lucky to come away with it. Not so lucky to come away with such big damage, but all in all, it was still okay."

title: 2026 F1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix - Baku Driver Ratings
excerpt:
Check out the full driver ratings for the 2026 F1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix!

27 September 10:40AM

George Russell returned to winning ways with a dominant victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix - a high-scoring affair in the latest driver ratings.

Who scored a nine despite not even finishing the race, who was "as bad as it gets" and which driver was firmly demolished by his team-mate, a Baku specialist?

Read on below to find out and let us know in the comments if you agree!

The top five

George Russell - 10

The rules here are simple. You get a grand chelem in a race, you get a 10. Only missed on topping FP3, but otherwise was unbeaten all weekend in every metric.

Max Verstappen - 9.5

Gets the benefit of the doubt in terms of the engine issue in qualifying and not getting his final lap due to Norris's yellow flag. Decisive early the race with the overtakes and made Russell work at the end, falling 0.196s short of stealing a win.

Isack Hadjar - 9.5

An excellent return to the cockpit, made even better by losing some time in FP1 with a car gremlin. Looked as if he had the pace to pass Verstappen at one point, but third was the best he could hope for and delivered.

Charles Leclerc - 9

Somehow got that Ferrari, with all its straight-line speed weaknesses onto the front row, and then did the best race that was expected, given the Red Bulls were so much stronger in race trim, as was Piastri before his Turn 1 mistake. Held off Antonelli by less than a half-a-second for fourth.

Pierre Gasly - 9

Qualified seventh, and beat Verstappen in the process, whatever his problems. Was consistently in the top 10 when it mattered through the weekend, and was on course for a big points haul until he got Colapinto'd.

© XPBimages

The bottom five

Alex Albon - 5

A decent enough qualifying and was doing his race until he crashed. Took full responsibility for it, but needless, although it did trigger the safety cars, which livened up a dull affair.

Lando Norris - 4.5

His worst performance for a while. Was never truly at one with the upgraded car all weekend, and was out-qualified by Piastri. Felt his MCL40 was different to Piastri's but was unlucky to be collateral damage in the Alpine vs Alpine disaster.

Lance Stroll - 4.5

Another weekend it is hard to judge Stroll given the woes of Aston Martin-Honda, so we go to qualifying. Stroll was nearly eight-tenths slower than Alonso in the other car, as the two-time champion out-qualified an engine-boosted Cadillac on the road.

Franco Colapinto - 4

Earns a mark back for his qualifying effort and getting into the top 10 and taking ninth, but barely. 'Out of control' was a phrase he used as he turned the Turn 1 braking zone into a bowling alley a la Bottas in Hungary 2021, whilst Flavio Briatore threatened "action" will be taken. Already bad enough, but doing what he did and taking out your team-mate from a solid double points position? As bad as it can get.

Valtteri Bottas - 3.5

Demolished by Perez all weekend. 1.6s slower in qualifying, and although he did not have the upgraded engine, it was not 1.6s worth of time. Crashed at the end and earned himself a trip to the stewards. One to forget.

title: Red Bull explain Max Verstappen Isack Hadjar Baku tactics after radio messages
excerpt:
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has explained why he did not order Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar to swap positions in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix despite the clear tyre issues affecting the four-time F1 champion.

From eighth on the grid, and with a fresh power unit from the pool in his RB22, Verstappen made up five places by the start of lap six as he scythed his way past Alpine's Pierre Gasly, Lewis Hamilton in his Ferrari, the McLaren of Lando Norris, the second Ferrari of Charles Leclerc, and team-mate Hadjar.

Next in line, McLaren's Oscar Piastri, proved a step too far, however, for Verstappen, who, instead, found himself with a seemingly quicker Hadjar directly behind him as the lap ticked by, given their offset in tyres, as the Dutchman was on the medium whilst the Frenchman was on the softs, which ultimately proved to be the better race tyre.

At times, Hadjar radioed across to indicate that he had pace, even asking at one stage whether Verstappen was struggling. He was told that he was "going through a bad phase with the tyres".

Instead of allowing Hadjar to attack Piastri, Red Bull opted to hold station with their drivers, hoping for a safety car that eventually arrived after 30 laps when Alex Albon buried his Williams in a barrier between Turns 5 & 6.

"We looked at all these scenarios, honestly, and we elected to hold the cars in that position," said Mekies, speaking to Sky Sports F1.

"We felt it was the best chance to get a chance [overtaking] at Piastri and at [George] Russell. It's very difficult here to not count on a safety car at some stage. We were all waiting for the safety car.

"Max was struggling with the medium at that stage, and we knew that on the soft we would have a better chance, and ultimately that's what happened."

[Article continues below]

Verstappen 'flying all weekend'

Through two safety car periods, Verstappen found himself in a position to hound Mercedes' Russell for the win, finishing just 0.196s adrift at the line after 51 laps, whilst Hadjar was third for his second podium of the year.

"We were missing one tenth, but we got the chance to fight with him [Russell] and to show we had the same pace," remarked Mekies, who felt that Verstappen was "flying all weekend".

"He was very, very strong," he added. "It was probably our strongest weekend. It was good to have the cars P2 and P3 on merit. Huge well done to everybody back in Milton Keynes.

"We had our upgrades here. It was massive work from everybody, chassis and PU side, to extract more out of the package.

"It felt very far away at the beginning of the season when the [other] guys were lapping a second faster than us, and we are in that fight now, so big well done to everyone."

title: George Russell fires rally cry after 'resilient' Mercedes fightback
excerpt:
George Russell believes he is now capable of fighting for grand prix wins "week in, week out" following a dominant performance at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

For the first time in his career, Russell posted a grand chelem after winning the Baku race from pole, having led all 51 laps, and set the fastest lap, defeating Max Verstappen by just 0.196s on the line.

The win, coupled with Kimi Antonelli's fifth-place has allowed Russell to cut his points deficit to 66 points after his third victory of the campaign.

Russell has been brutally honest at times in 2026 about his struggles in gelling his driving style to the W17 machine, but since the summer break, has scored three podiums, including the win, and also bagged the Sprint victory in the Netherlands.

Reflecting after the win, the closest in F1 since the 2002 United States GP between Rubens Barrichello and Michael Schumacher, Russell felt that driving the car was "finally coming to me more intuitively."

"I’m very proud of the resilience that I and my close group of engineers have shown during the tough periods this year because there’s been a lot of hard work to overcome some of the challenges and to adapt my driving style to suit this new car better," Russell told media, including RacingNews365.

"F1 is so tough, you don’t get opportunities to practice this, and finally it’s coming to me a bit more intuitively than it once did, and I’m gaining confidence, especially on circuits like this; it just allows you to eke out that little bit more on the brakes, get that little bit closer to the walls, and it’s been a flawless weekend.

"I never lost that faith in myself; even through tough moments, I knew there was a reason why I was off the pace.

"It wasn’t like I just suddenly forgot how to drive, and I knew I would be able to find it again. I just had to be patient. So, I feel confident. You know, it’s been four races since the break.

"I’ve been on the front row in three of them, three podiums from the four races. I feel I can fight for victory week in, week out now."

The article continues below.

Russell vs Verstappen

After the second safety car restart, Verstappen tried to hunt Russell down, and was just 0.196s behind at the line, in the 10th closest green-flag finish in the history of F1.

Making a restart from the lead was a new situation for Russell - as he detailed his thought process.

"It's the first restart I’ve done this season from the lead. These power units are very challenging at restarts, getting the battery in the right place for turbo spinning at the right speed, and I always do good preparation on what I want to do at a restart," he said.

"It needs a lot more thought into it than ever before. But I was keeping an eye on my mirrors where Max was, and I had waited for that moment when the gap was just slightly larger and managed to break him because I knew if he saw half a chance, he would have been sending it down the inside.

"So, I was pleased with it."

title: Lando Norris handed 'too harsh' judgment over Franco Colapinto ban remark
excerpt:
George Russell has pushed back on Lando Norris' call for Franco Colapinto to be handed a one-race ban after the Argentine wiped out Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and the McLaren driver at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto lost control of his car into Turn 1 during the lap 36 safety car restart at the Baku City Circuit, spearing into Gasly, who was then pushed into Norris on the outside line. All three drivers retired on the spot.

The stewards handed Colapinto a 10-second time penalty for causing the collision. Because he retired before the sanction could be served, it is set to be converted into a grid penalty for next weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, though the exact number of places has not yet been confirmed.

Norris declared publicly that the incident deserved a race ban. Race-winner Russell and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who finished second, disagreed.

"I think that's too harsh," said Russell, speaking to the media, including RacingNews365. "Personally, [with] safety car restarts, cold tyres, a very small mistake can have big consequences, and from what I saw, that's what it looked like. It was a small error that had a big consequence."

"Race bans should come from drivers intentionally doing something very dangerous and very reckless. I think it was unfortunate."

[Article continues below]

Verstappen - As long as he's aware

Verstappen, who finished just 0.196s behind Russell, also weighed in, saying accountability from the driver at fault mattered more than a suspension.

"As long as the driver who caused it is aware of what he did and apologises," said Verstappen. Colapinto did apologise.

"I mean, that happens, like a small mistake or a misjudgment. You lock up. It's on the inside, low grip.

"It's unfortunate that it involves so many cars, but unfortunately it happens, and it's not nice for anyone involved.

"But as George said, a race ban is probably a bit much."

title: Lewis Hamilton hits back after Ferrari Baku disappointment: 'Why would I agree?'
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has hit back at being asked if Ferrari has fallen to fourth in the pecking order following a disappointing Azerbaijan Grand Prix, questioning "why would I agree?"

Hamilton finished sixth in Baku, unable to make progress on the circuit's long straights as Ferrari's power unit deficit continued to bite.

The seven-time world champion qualified sixth, but slipped away from the podium fight once the lights went out.

Hamilton crossed the line 22.382s behind race winner Russell, with Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar completing the podium places for Red Bull.

Baku's 2.2-kilometre full-throttle blast has proven a brutal proving ground for straight-line speed all season, and Ferrari's known top-speed shortfall left Hamilton stranded between cars rather than in genuine contention.

Briefly discussing his race, Hamilton told select media, including RacingNews365: "Yeah, I was in no man's time most of the time."

That isolation reflected a wider issue for the Scuderia. Ferrari has publicly acknowledged a straight-line speed deficit this season, with technical director-level admissions pointing to power unit shortfalls compared to Mercedes, even as the SF-26 chassis remains competitive through the corners.

Asked how it felt not being able to do anything when defending on the straight, Hamilton replied: "It's not great, but it is what it is. There's not very much I can do."

Lewis Hamilton pins Ferrari third in F1 pecking order

The result leaves Ferrari facing familiar questions about where it sits in the constructors' fight, with Mercedes and Red Bull both clearly ahead on pace at Baku.

Ferrari has continued development work on the SF-26 rather than pivoting fully to 2027, with a further upgrade package expected before the season is out.

But Hamilton was in no mood to accept a bleaker reading of the team's current form when it was put to him that Ferrari had dropped to fourth in the order.

Discussing whether Ferrari has slipped to fourth in the pecking order, Hamilton snapped back: "What's the importance of that? Why would I agree with it?

"I mean, I don't know where we are. Third or second? I don't know. We're obviously not the second quickest at the moment, but we're ahead of McLaren today, so maybe we're third."

title: Max Verstappen branded 'shark' after sniffing George Russell 'blood in the water'
excerpt:
Max Verstappen was like a shark sniffing George Russell's blood in the water during the dying moments of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, according to Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord.

Russell was strolling to a comfortable victory at the Baku City Circuit, but two safety car disruptions erased his advantage.

When the racing resumed in anger, the Briton could not shake off Verstappen, who took the chequered flag just under two tenths of a second behind Russell.

"It was all unfolding exactly as we'd hoped in our most optimistic strategy plan," Lord reflected to Sky Sports F1.

"George was just able to break away at the front, build the gap, was completely in control, and then after that restart, suddenly, Max got a sniff.

"It's like a shark with blood in the water, and suddenly there he is, and George could gain half a second every time in the middle sector. Then, like a big bungee cord, it just pulled Max back in the slipstream.

"So, high, high pressure for George. One mistake, and that would have been the win gone, and he didn't make any at all."

Mercedes 'blood pressure rocketed'

To add further stress to the high-stakes scenario, Valtteri Bottas crashing at Turn 15 left one final hurdle for Russell, who also lost his boost, to overcome.

It left the Mercedes pit wall reeling, despite the 28-year-old successfully claiming his eighth grand prix victory.

"And even on the last lap, our blood pressure rocketed when we saw Valtteri in the wall and a double yellow," Lord added.

"George said he'd lost boost, and it looked like it might be lost at the very last, but fortunately, it wasn't. So, two tenths, but two tenths was enough."
